state.problem: A weather balloon holds 12 cubic meters of helium on the ground, where the air temperature is 27 degrees Celsius. As it climbs the temperature falls to -3 degrees Celsius and the balloon is free to change volume, keeping its internal pressure equal to the outside air pressure. Treating the helium's volume as proportional to its absolute temperature, what volume does the balloon occupy aloft, in cubic meters?

observations.summary: 12 cubic meters of helium at 27 degrees Celsius will expand to 12 cubic meters of helium at -3 degrees Celsius. The volume of a gas is proportional to its temperature in Kelvin, so the volume of the balloon at -3 degrees Celsius will be 12 cubic meters * (273.15 K - 3 degrees Celsius) / 273.15 K = 12 cubic meters * 1 = 12 cubic meters.
